title: Week 26 Mastery Quiz

questions.question: Which definition best matches “externality”?
options: A supporter of ratifying the Constitution and strengthening national government.
An organized collection demonstrating research, reasoning, participation, revision, and reflection.
A cost or benefit imposed on a third party and not fully reflected in a transaction price.
The quantities producers are willing and able to sell at different prices during a stated period.
questions.explanation: Externality means a cost or benefit imposed on a third party and not fully reflected in a transaction price.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “public good”?
options: A good that is difficult to exclude people from and can be used without substantially reducing availability to others.
Ability to produce more output with the same resources.
An opponent or critic of ratification who feared centralized power and demanded stronger protections for liberty.
Allocation of legislative, executive, and judicial authority to different branches.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “common resource”?
options: A resource that is difficult to exclude users from but can be depleted by use.
Human time, effort, skill, and knowledge used in production.
The accumulated outstanding federal borrowing resulting from past deficits and other financing operations.
The condition that available resources are insufficient to satisfy every possible want.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “free rider”?
options: A person who benefits from a good or action without contributing to its cost.
The principle that public officials and private persons are governed by publicly known law.
Intentional different treatment based on a protected characteristic.
A rule that government generally may regulate expression without favoring or suppressing a viewpoint.

options: The value of the best alternative forgone when a choice is made.
A tax intended to align private incentives with an external social cost.
The process by which agencies create regulations under statutory authority.
A government document, dataset, proceeding, or other record available for public inspection.

questions.question: Which definition best matches “cap-and-trade”?
options: Public programs pooling risks such as unemployment, disability, health cost, or old-age income.
A system limiting total emissions and allowing permits to be traded.
A professional public workforce selected and managed through established personnel systems.
Output measured at current prices.
